subject: Tenant data classification, egress gating & subprocessor approval — onboarding Qs
messages:
From: Ellis Moore <ellis.moore@clarityhealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Clarity Health Security <security@clarityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifications on tenant data classification + egress gating (SSQ attached)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we appreciated the detail on isolation and routing. Security flagged a few areas in the security questionnaire (attached) where we need concrete answers before legal proceeds with the DPA annex. High-level asks: 

- How do you classify tenant-level PII vs aggregated telemetry? (we need a mapping we can attach to our DPA)
- For cross-tenant exports, is there an approval workflow and can exports be scoped to specific fields?
- Who are your subprocessors that could have access to decrypted content for support/repairs? We need roles and residency for each.

I've attached the SSQ (clarity-ssq-v2.xlsx) and a rough tenant-dataflow diagram we sketched for reference. Can you loop in the right folks on your side?

Thanks,
Ellis
Ellis Moore
Head of InfoSec, Clarity Health
ellis.moore@clarityhealth.com

Attachments: clarity-ssq-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), tenant-dataflow-egress-diagram-v1.png (image)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Moore <ellis.moore@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on tenant data classification + egress gating (SSQ attached)

Hi Ellis — thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. Forwarding answers inline below and attaching an annotated dataflow. Looping in Ben (security engineering) and Marissa (privacy/onboarding) for the DPA and subprocessor details.

Inline answers (quick summary):
1) Classification: We maintain a tenant data classification map that distinguishes four tiers: 
   - Tier A: Direct identifiers (names, national ids, full PII)
   - Tier B: Sensitive attributes (health-related flags, special categories)
   - Tier C: Pseudonymized identifiers (hashed tokens, reversible only with KMS access)
   - Tier D: Aggregated/telemetry (non-identifiable metrics)
   I'll attach a CSV export of the mapping and a short mapping table in the Drive link.

2) Exports & egress gating: Exports are gated via our console + API. Exports that include Tier A/B fields require a two-step approval: (a) request with justification (logged), (b) approval by an admin with "export:approve" role. We support field-level scoping; we can create export filters to remove specific PII fields pre-export. You can see this in the attached annotated diagram (tenant-dataflow-egress-diagram-v1.png).

3) Subprocessors: We maintain a public subprocessor roster and internal access matrix. Short list relevant to your ask:
   - EdgeOps LLC — responsible for edge routing and caching (no plaintext PII access; only hashed tokens), US 
   - VectorCompute — GPU inference providers for hosted models (access to plaintext optional depending on workload; covered by our DPA annex and KMS envelope keys), US/EU
   - AuditLog Inc — stores immutable telemetry logs (pseudonymized; can store full traces only with customer opt-in)

Ben/Marissa — can you confirm the residency and whether VectorCompute has any support access that would allow decryption of stored content? Also attaching a proposed DPA annex with redlines for clarity.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: tenant-dataflow-egress-diagram-v1-annotated.png (image), dpa-annex-proposed-redlines.docx (doc)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ellis Moore <ellis.moore@clarityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on tenant data classification + egress gating (SSQ attached)

Sofia / Marissa — quick security confirmation and a suggested gating tweak for Clarity's SSQ.

- Residency & support access: VectorCompute (our inference partner) operates in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for this customer. They have no automatic decryption rights: any ability to view plaintext requires an explicit ephemeral KMS grant scoped per-job. We enforce ephemeral grants for debugging and require recorded approval. I'll add a short note to the DPA annex wording to make that explicit.

- Audit trail: All export requests, approvals, and artifact retrievals are immutably logged and retained for 2 years by default; retention can be increased per contract (addendum). Logs include requestor, fields requested, and the export hash.

- Suggested export gating tweak: For customers with regulated data (like Clarity Health), we recommend a policy that constrains export runs to a dedicated "export-approval" role that cannot be combined with "support:decrypt" role for the same user. This prevents admin/MITM overlap. We can enforce via RBAC in the Console.

Marissa — I attached a short redline to the annex doc (dpa-annex-proposed-redlines.docx) clarifying ephemeral grants and export approval workflow. If legal is OK, we can formalize the 2-step export gating and sign the annex.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: dpa-annex-proposed-redlines.docx (annotated)

From: Ellis Moore <ellis.moore@clarityhealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-07T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on tenant data classification + egress gating (SSQ attached)

Sofia / Ben / Marissa — appreciate the fast turnaround and the level of detail. A few quick follow-ups before we kick legal: 

- Can you produce the CSV export of the classification map (Sofia mentioned) and drop it in the shared Drive link? We need to attach it to the DPA annex.
- Please confirm VectorCompute's support process (ticket only, no shell access) in writing for our vendor risk team.
- For the export approvals: can you set a default that requires two distinct approvers for any Tier A/B export (we prefer two-person control)? If so, include that clause in the annex language.

If you can get those three items done by end of day Friday, we'll route to legal and procurement and circulate DocuSign.

Thanks,
Ellis
